chen_2012.citation: Chen Y, Zhou L, Yuan L, Zhang Z-h, Liu X, Wu Q. Formulation, characterization, and evaluation of in vitro skin permeation and in vivo pharmacodynamics of surface-charged tripterine-loaded nanostructured lipid carriers. International Journal of Nanomedicine. 2012;7:3023-3033.
chen_2012.study_objective: Evaluate the effect of surface charge on in vitro skin permeation and in vivo pharmacodynamics of tripterine-loaded NLCs; optimize for skin disease treatment.

formulation_composition.cationic_NLC: stearylamine 180 mg; IPM 60 mg; soybean lecithin 30 mg; TPGS 30 mg; Pluronic F68 1.0 wt% in aqueous surfactant solution
formulation_composition.neutral_NLC: glyceryl behenate 180 mg; MCTs 60 mg; soybean lecithin 30 mg; TPGS 30 mg; Pluronic F68 1.0 wt%
formulation_composition.anionic_NLC: Precirol ATO-5 180 mg; IPM 60 mg; soybean lecithin 30 mg; TPGS 30 mg; Pluronic F68 1.0 wt%
formulation_composition.drug: loaded NLCs prepared to contain 15 mg tripterine

chen_2012.lipids: Glyceryl behenate; Precirol ATO-5; IPM; MCTs; soybean lecithin
chen_2012.surfactants: d-alpha-tocopherol polyethylene glycol succinate (TPGS); Pluronic F68
chen_2012.surface_modifications: Surface charge classes: cationic, neutral, anionic
chen_2012.PDI: NOT REPORTED in the visible line-cited extract
chen_2012.zeta_potential: NOT REPORTED in the visible line-cited extract
chen_2012.drug_loading: 15 mg tripterine used; drug loading percentage: NOT REPORTED
chen_2012.release_profile: Delayed tripterine release; release-order statement in abstract is qualitative. Kinetics fit to zero-order, first-order, Higuchi, Ritger-Peppas; FIRST-ORDER selected (good correlation).
chen_2012.stability: NOT REPORTED as a storage time-series in the visible line-cited extract
chen_2012.crystallinity: Tripterine was in the amorphous state in the surface-charged NLCs
chen_2012.cell_models: HaCaT normal human skin cells; B16BL6 melanoma cells
chen_2012.animal_models: Male Sprague-Dawley rats (skin permeation); male C57BL/6 mice (melanoma pharmacodynamics)
chen_2012.disease_model: Melanoma-bearing mice; treatment aim also states skin diseases
chen_2012.tissue_model: Full-thickness abdominal skin of young male Sprague-Dawley rats; skin sections 0-30, 30-60, 60-90 um
chen_2012.uptake: Cellular uptake in HaCaT and B16BL6 assessed; order cationic > neutral > anionic
chen_2012.toxicity: In vitro cytotoxicity on B16BL6 evaluated; cationic NLCs highest inhibition ratio in B16BL6. Systemic toxicity: NOT REPORTED in the visible line-cited extract
chen_2012.process_conditions: preparation in aqueous surfactant solution at 65 C; stabilization at 0-2 C; release/permeation experiments at 37 C; receptor media PBS pH 7.4 in defined solvent mixtures
chen_2012.limitations: Independent validation: NOT REPORTED. Human tissue model: NOT REPORTED. Storage stability time-series: NOT REPORTED. Precipitation/aggregation kinetics: NOT REPORTED.

wang_2025.citation: Wang F, Lai W, Xie D, Zhou M, Wang J, Xu R, Zhang R, Li G. Nanoparticle-mediated celastrol ER targeting delivery amplify immunogenic cell death in melanoma. Journal of Advanced Research. 2025;71:585-601.
wang_2025.evidence_level: PRIMARY_ARTICLE_PREVIEW (article-page/abstract level, not full PDF extraction)
wang_2025.study_objective: Construct ER-targeted nanoparticles to amplify celastrol-mediated immunogenic cancer cell death and improve immune response.
wang_2025.formulation_composition: TSE-CEL/NP self-assembled using PLGA loaded with celastrol as a hydrophobic core and p-tosylethylenediamine (TSE) modified DSPE-PEG as surface material. Exact mass ratios: NOT REPORTED.
wang_2025.lipids: DSPE-PEG (surface material); other lipid components: NOT REPORTED
wang_2025.drug_loading: Celastrol-loaded PLGA core reported; numerical loading value: NOT REPORTED
wang_2025.animal_models: Unilateral and bilateral tumor models; lung metastasis B16F10 melanoma tumor-bearing mice. Exact strain: NOT REPORTED
wang_2025.tissue_model: Endoplasmic reticulum targeting in tumor cells; tumor microenvironment in vivo
wang_2025.biodistribution: ER accumulation reported qualitatively; organ-level biodistribution: NOT REPORTED
wang_2025.uptake: TSE-CEL/NP specially accumulated in ER; flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, TEM, immunofluorescence used to evaluate ER targeting and immunogenic tumor cell death
wang_2025.mechanism_reported: ER localization -> ER stress -> CRT/HMGB1/ATP release -> DC recruitment/maturation -> CD8+ T-cell activation -> antitumor & anti-metastasis response
wang_2025.limitations: Particle size, zeta, EE, in vivo PK, storage stability, precipitation/aggregation data: NOT REPORTED

shukla_2020.citation: Shukla SK, Chan A, Parvathaneni V, Kanabar DD, Patel K, Ayehunie S, Muth A, Gupta V. Enhanced solubility, stability, permeation and anti-cancer efficacy of Celastrol-beta-cyclodextrin inclusion complex. Journal of Molecular Liquids. 2020;318:113936.
shukla_2020.study_objective: Investigate complexation of celastrol with FDA-approved beta-cyclodextrin derivatives; evaluate complexation efficiency, binding affinity, thermodynamic stability, physiological stability, permeability, and therapeutic activity.
shukla_2020.formulation_composition: Celastrol; 2-hydroxypropyl-beta-cyclodextrin (HP-betaCD; avg degree of substitution 4.5; avg MW 1426 g/mol); sulfobutylether-beta-cyclodextrin sodium salt (SBE-betaCD; Dexolve; avg degree of substitution 6.5; avg MW 2163 g/mol). Exact molar complexation ratio in the visible preview: NOT REPORTED.
shukla_2020.stabilizers: beta-cyclodextrin derivatives as complexing/solubilizing agents; separate stabilizer field: NOT REPORTED
shukla_2020.stability: Celastrol stability greatly increased in PBS (pH 7.4) and in rat plasma and human plasma upon complexation with SBE-betaCD
shukla_2020.crystallinity: FTIR, 1H NMR, PXRD, and DSC confirmed inclusion complex formation
shukla_2020.solubility: Aqueous solubility of celastrol increased 30-fold after complexation with SBE-betaCD vs intrinsic solubility. Celastrol is a BCS class IV drug with very low solubility and intestinal permeability.
shukla_2020.time_series: NOT REPORTED in the visible preview
shukla_2020.cell_models: Human lung cancer cells; exact cell line name in the visible preview: NOT REPORTED
shukla_2020.animal_models: NOT REPORTED in the visible preview
shukla_2020.disease_model: Human non-small cell lung cancer in vitro
shukla_2020.tissue_model: EpiIntestinal 3D small intestine tissue model for permeability
shukla_2020.toxicity: Paper states celastrol has severe adverse effects (hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, cardiotoxicity) as general background; comparative toxicity of the complex in vivo: NOT REPORTED in the visible preview
shukla_2020.limitations: Nanoparticle-specific size/PDI/zeta fields absent (inclusion complex, not a nanoparticle paper in the visible preview). In vivo PK, precipitation, aggregation, storage time-series: NOT REPORTED

sun_2024.pmid_pmcid: PMCID not directly visible in the opened text; NOT REPORTED here

sun_2024.study_objective: Review efficiency-enhancing and toxicity-reducing celastrol delivery strategies; classify into direct chemical modification and indirect physical connection delivery systems.
sun_2024.classification: dendrimers, polymers, albumins, vesicular carriers, aptamer conjugates, glucolipid conjugates
sun_2024.key_statements: Celastrol has low bioavailability, poor water solubility, off-target cytotoxicity; reviewed delivery technologies improve selectivity by covalent bonding or encapsulation.

stability_and_precipitation_section.aggregation_mechanisms: Chen 2012 NOT REPORTED; Wang 2025 NOT REPORTED; Shukla 2020 NOT REPORTED
stability_and_precipitation_section.crystallization: Chen 2012: tripterine amorphous in surface-charged NLCs. Shukla 2020: FTIR/1H NMR/PXRD/DSC confirm inclusion-complex formation (not an NP crystallization time-series). Wang 2025: NOT REPORTED
stability_and_precipitation_section.degradation: Chen 2012 NOT REPORTED; Shukla 2020: celastrol stability greatly increased in PBS pH 7.4 and rat/human plasma upon SBE-betaCD complexation; Wang 2025 NOT REPORTED
stability_and_precipitation_section.oxidation: NOT REPORTED in the reviewed primary papers
stability_and_precipitation_section.hydrolysis: NOT REPORTED in the reviewed primary papers

stability_and_precipitation_section.pH_effects: Chen receptor media PBS pH 7.4 in defined solvent mixtures; Shukla 2020 increased stability in PBS pH 7.4 after complexation. pH-dependent kinetic curves across multiple pH values: NOT REPORTED
stability_and_precipitation_section.temperature_effects: Chen preparation 65 C; stabilization 0-2 C; experiments 37 C. Temperature-dependent stability outcomes: NOT REPORTED
stability_and_precipitation_section.encapsulated_vs_released: Chen: delayed release + enhanced skin permeation, no released-drug precipitation model. Shukla: improved stability/permeability after complexation, no released-drug precipitation kinetics.
